promptLatex: How many positive integer solutions does x + y + z + w = 12 have?
hintLatex:
For positive solutions, give one unit to each variable first. This uses 4 units, leaving 12 - 4 = 8 units to distribute freely among 4 variables.
The formula is \binom{n-1}{k-1} = \binom{12-1}{4-1} = \binom{11}{3}.
solutionLatex:
Give one unit to each of the 4 variables first, using 4 units. Then distribute the remaining 12 - 4 = 8 units freely among 4 variables (nonnegative solutions).

Number of ways: \binom{8+4-1}{4-1} = \binom{11}{3} = \frac{11 \times 10 \times 9}{6} = 165.
